boundary_form: Each work carries a START locus only, in the volume's own served loci. The script assigns every row from one start up to the next, so the partition is exact by construction and no gap or overlap is expressible. That matters most for the longest work: in v7pt1 item IX is 86% of the volume, and a range with an explicit end would let a one-page slip there mis-file more text than every other boundary combined.
lemma_policy: A commentary that quotes its base text inline as lemmata is one work, not a work plus a citation of another. Item IX quotes Hermogenes peri staseon, which is served separately; those lemmata count toward item IX's own tokens.
locus_policy: Target loci key to the PRINTED Walz page (issue #15), derived arithmetically as scan - offset, and keep the source row ordinal: printed 34 row 9 becomes 34.9. The ordinal is not renumbered per work, because two works share printed page 34 and renumbering would put both at 34.1 and stop the ordinal meaning a line on the page. pages_pg.json is deliberately NOT consulted per page: it misreads roughly 14 folios in this volume.
rank_policy: A treatise this corpus already serves as primary from a better edition becomes a secondary witness (issue #14). Nothing in v7pt1 is so served, so every work here is primary and the carve moves no tokens out of the published primary figure.
tlg_policy: A tlg id is asserted only where the vendored canon carries a record keyed to this edition ("Rhetores Graeci, vol. 7.1"). Four of the nine rest on title plus word-count proximity in Rabe, which is not evidence, so they ship with tlg null rather than a guess that would read as a fact in tlg_crosswalk.json.

volumes.basis: A second carve of the same volume, taking the Hermogenean block its first carve deferred. Every boundary is a display title read off the Internet Archive scan rhetoresgraeciem03walzuoft, because in this volume the running head lags its title page by two or three pages and the OCR captures the head far more reliably than the title. Using the heads alone would have put three of the four boundaries late.
volumes.disposition_note: All four are served from First1KGreek and become secondary witnesses under #14. The text corroborates it: 4-gram overlap runs 37.4% to 43.3%.
volumes.edition_title: Rhetores Graeci, vol. III, ed. C. Walz (Stuttgart/Tubingen, Cotta, 1834)
volumes.front_matter_note: scans 0007-0014, the volume's ARGUMENTUM and Latin front matter, 616 tokens. Left in the volume file.
volumes.offset_note: printed = scan - 14, the same offset the volume's first carve used, re-confirmed here against the scan: page 191 sits on scan 205 and page 403 on scan 417. A '149' printed at the corner of the Peri methodou title page is a marginal reference to another edition, not a Walz page number; the two anchors either side of it both give 14.
volumes.trailing_residual_note: printed 748 onward, the corrigenda and index rows the volume's first carve left behind. The Hermogenean block ends with ΤΕΛΟΣ ΕΡΜΟΓΕΝΟΥΣ at printed 445, and nothing between that and here survived the first pass.

works.incipit_note: Anchored on the treatise's opening words, not its title. The initial epsilon is left out because the OCR reads Εἰπερ for Εἴπερ.
